quote_text: how big a sigh of relief of this this victory was from various point of view like test a test series in Sri Lanka Galle test always considered as a tough tough assignment and from the WTC point of view. >> I wouldn't say sigh of relief we just happy and every test match victory is special. We coming back to Sri Lanka after a long time so a lot of the guys haven't been here and yeah so it's a it's a great start to the tour. I think we take most of the boxes and and we did most of the things right that we spoke about before the test match and the way we prepared I think we could put that into practice and put that into the game so that was really good to see and I think this victory will obviously give a sense of happiness that we did the right things and also give us a confidence going into the next game and also we have a big home series coming up in India next year so yeah just understanding against spin and playing in spinning conditions is something that we've all been working on so and from that point of view it gives us a lot of happiness here. >> You talked about working on playing in spin conditions you also posted some videos around you know doing the homework in regards to your batting and most of the players have come here prepared well prepared before playing the warm up match so these these homeworks little bit of detailing in the batting or bowling part how important is it when you you know go outside India or even play in India in this particular format for younger generations and those who are coming newly into the team also. >> I think for me personally it it is the most important thing I think even before the series even before you come to a test match venue I think how well prepared you are uh gives you the best chance to do well in in any conditions whether it's in India or outside of India just being prepared just doing your homework, not just about the wickets, just about some of the bowlers that you're going to face. Um going back and watching some of the the games that have been played in Sri Lanka, and what phase of the game as a batter do you get a lot of runs? What game What phase of the game do you have to soak in the pressure? When do you have to attack? When do you have to um be slightly cautious? These are some of the things that um for me personally as a player, I've always liked um doing that and ticking those boxes. That's a big part of my preparation. And um um I think that that's something that's really helped me in in all the test matches that I've played. Yes, not always will you get success, but I think there's a bare minimum for someone playing at this level um to to do before you come for a test series. And um I think yeah, that's that's something that I I strong strongly recommend to um everyone that I play with or anyone who's watching. >> Okay, so your views on Devdutt Padikkal's innings, and uh what was the conversation yesterday when um you took the DRS? You were going back, and Devdutt said what was the conversation then? >> Um yeah, firstly on his innings, I think um uh that innings was I think for me um the defining part of this test match. Uh I know the way he batted, the tempo that he batted with, and to go on and get a big 100 in the first innings really set up the game for us. Um the conditions were really hot and um you know, it was challenging physically as well. So, for him to um you know, get through that, and you know, firstly to get his first 100 is a special moment, but to go on from there and get a big 100 and uh stitch partnerships with different players, and get uh get a big first innings total really set up this test match. So, that was really pleasing and um someone who I've uh you know played a lot of cricket with and seen him grow up and come from Bangalore and play for Karnataka as a was really happy to be there and to see and to witness his first hundred and hopefully carries this confidence into the next game and into his test career as well. The conversation there was obviously I mean you would have seen the video I was walking walking back and I felt like it was it was out the only doubt that I had was did I get outside the line but he said no I don't think it's outside the line but I think it might be high. And then he said might as well be a three review so just take it I think it might be a little high. So I reluctantly took it and then when it happened to be missing then obviously I didn't get too many runs after that but yeah. When you get chances like that as a batter it's it's like a it's a gift it's a second innings and second chance and little disappointed that I couldn't convert it but yeah it was a sweet moment. >> KL you've played many different roles in different formats. When you're going out to bat now in a test match and when you're building an innings and batting it for a long time how are you feeling at the moment? >> Feeling good I'm feeling like I'm like I just said I think most of the work is how I prepared before coming into a test series and that's something in the last few years I think I've paid a lot of attention to and and really worked hard before entering a test series whether it's mental makeup or whether it's doing the physical hours and whether it's you know batting preparing in a way where you know the conditions will be suitable to where I'm going so done that and worked really hard with my coaches back home Um, and that has given me um you know, clarity in in in the way I want to play, um in the way I want to build an innings, and um how I want to counter certain type of bowlers, how I want to play in a in a in seeming conditions or spinning conditions or or a good wicket. So, those those are something that uh those are things that I've worked on, and um yeah, um since I've been doing that and and feeling confident in that, I think um I carry that um calmness into every test match because I feel like I've done all of those things right, and um and having played 50-60 odd test matches, you know that that's the thing that you need to um control most, which is in your control, and I can go there and get get a first bowler, but um you know, there's a sense of balance and calmness now that after I've played so many test matches, when I walk into a test match. >> Rahul, especially in the first innings, you were there when the ball was new and hard, and then you were also there when it got softer. Uh what are the adjustments that you as a set batter have to make when you go from this phase to that phase? And also from that same token, when you're fielding at slip or something and watching the ball lose uh hardness when your spinners are bowling, what kind of messaging do you give out to those guys then? >> Yeah, it was um I think the the pattern from day one was pretty similar, whether you know, we bowled or or the Sri Lankan team bowled the new ball, obviously, for the first 20-25 overs, felt like um uh the spinners got a lot more purchase off the wicket. Um and then as the ball started getting older, um uh um can't say got slightly easier, but uh you as a batter, you weren't worried about the ball skidding through or you know, hitting your front pad. So, I think that um sort of makes the batter's life a little bit easier when you're not worried about one mode of dismissal. Whereas in the first 25-30 overs, you felt like ball could go straight and you can get LBW on the inside or if the ball spins, you can get caught behind on the outside. So, that puts a lot of doubts in the batter's mind. But, um yeah, every batter that could go through that first, uh 20-25 balls in in their own individual innings and if they could soak up that pressure, um it's like it got it got easier as you batted and you know, you could figure out a way to score runs. Maybe this wicket was slightly, um different to, you know, uh wickets that we play in in India or in in in England and Australia where, you know, the ball's spinning. So, you score in different areas of the game uh of the ground. So, once a batter figured that out, felt like it was an even contest. The bowlers also felt a bit of pressure to get batters out when they were, you know, when they were put under pressure. So, yeah, it was Yeah, the messaging was when we were fielding was clear that, you know, there's help in the wicket. So, how how long could we keep putting the ball in in the area where the batters are finding it hard and uh how patient can we be? And um the batters are going to score or play a few shots, but can we keep bowling the ball in those areas and be patient and hope for the batter to make a mistake or for one one ball to spin more than the the other ball and get that edge. So, it was about patience and I think we we were able to do that and um you know, Jaddu obviously is so experienced. He was there. So, they came along with Kuldeep and Manav obviously had their own own plans and they were always talking to each other as to the pace, uh what pace to bowl at, when to bowl slow, when to bowl quicker, whether to bowl fuller or shorter. So, they had a good good sort of like communication in between and that really helped us. >> Uh KL, uh both Padikkal and uh, Manish Pandey both in their first kind of few test matches, but here had, you know, in an away test, uh, played lead roles, uh, for for India. What is it about the team environment that, you know, allows players to have impact like that and and what did you see the two of them do uh, specially to allow them to have that kind of impact in this game? >> Yeah, I think um, a lot of credit goes to how um, our first-class setup is is done and how some of these guys are India A structure that's been there for the at least I know for the last few years the the teams are touring to countries that we're going to play in um, a couple of months before. So, Devdutt was here um, a month or 6 weeks before the test series and played a couple of games there and then we played a practice game here. So, got used to those conditions. Um, so yeah, but once you sort of put players in those positions and give them the exposure and and the experience that they need at at at that level, I feel like that um, really helps them understand what they need to do when they come into into into the national team and they're um, better prepared and give themselves a better chance to do well at this level. It's not like you go from playing um, Ranji Trophy cricket straight into an Indian Indian Indian team and and a test match in in a couple of months time where that difference is huge. The standard from there to here is it's a big jump. So, then sometimes players are, you know, are found wanting and they need to, you know, they need to figure their game at an international level and when there's already so much pressure, that becomes hard sometimes, but because of these um, because of the struct the way Indian cricket is structured and first-class cricket is structured, I feel like that's, you know, [snorts] they they they go from first-class Ranji Trophy to playing India A, a lot of India A games, and they toured Australia, Sri Lanka, England, all of these places. So, you know, it helps them get better at their game and understand their game. And by the time they've got their Test cap, they're, you know, well aware of their own game and the expectations of playing at international cricket and what they can do to do well here. So, I think a lot of credit goes to that. And obviously, they're all special players. They've done well um for their states and scored runs or taken a lot of wickets. They're special players and have the skill, but helping them with, you know, giving them the right opportunities and sending them to the right places to play cricket and test their own game, I think gets them ready for international cricket. Um and that's that's what's helped the Indian team in the last few years. >> Just a couple of last few questions for you. >> KL, during every net session, we see you talk a lot with the younger batters in the team, whether that's Jaiswal, Dhruv. Devdutt spoke how much he looks up to you when it comes to batting. And Dhruv and Jaiswal have also spoken in similar lines. So, just talk about that role which you are naturally kind of taking in the group of being that elder elder person and just guiding the young batters around. And you were the surviving batter from the last lot which played a Test here. So, how much is that kind of playing up on your mind? And how consciously do you look forward to that just to kind of get that knowledge transfer going when it comes to the younger group who are just finding their feet now? >> No, look, I've been asked this question like many times in the last few months, and I don't think I'm doing anything special. I think it's just every player's responsibility to to help another player out. And whether you're older or or even someone who's just 26 but played 20 Test matches, it's everybody's responsibility to, you know, help your your fellow teammates out. And um the dressing room here is always, I've said this before as well, the atmosphere always has been a place where, you know, players are are are open to helping um other players and working with them on their batting or just mindset and just telling them what to expect in Sri Lanka, what to expect in New Zealand, what to expect um in in, you know, wherever we we travel to. So, uh that's something that I've always done. It's not just because these guys have come in and they're younger, even when we had um players who played 60, 70 test matches and I only played 20 or 30 test matches, there was no there was no shame or there was no uh uh sort of egos in players to say no, I played more test matches than you, so I can't learn something from you or there's no um feeling for me to say no, he's played so many test matches, so I can't go and talk to him. So, it was always been an open open dressing room and, you know, people are learning from each other, you know, I might learn a thing or two from from a newer player.
